tax_010:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for claiming the federal R&D tax credit (Form 6765) by scoping our eligibility and building a comparison of R&D tax credit study providers. Please do NOT select a vendor or commit to anything — this is a preparation step only.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already known: our company name/domain, incorporation date, whether we're pre-revenue, approximate annual gross receipts for the last few years, headcount, and a rough description of our technical/engineering work (product features, R&D activities, experiments, prototypes) so we can gauge qualified research expense (QRE) eligibility.

Then:
1. Summarize in plain language whether we likely qualify for the R&D credit and the payroll-tax offset (Form 8974), based on IRS criteria for qualified research (technological in nature, eliminating uncertainty, process of experimentation, business component test) and the payroll-offset eligibility rules (gross receipts under $5M, and no gross receipts more than 5 years ago).
2. Research and list at least 4-6 reputable R&D tax credit study providers (e.g., specialized R&D tax credit firms, national accounting firms with R&D practices, and software-driven R&D credit services). For each, pull from their websites/public info: pricing model (flat fee, % of credit, hourly), typical turnaround time, audit-defense support/guarantee, client reviews or case studies, and any stated specialization in startups/pre-revenue companies.
3. Build a comparison table with these columns: Provider, Pricing Model, Est. Cost, Audit Defense, Turnaround, Startup Focus, Notable Reviews.
4. Flag any red flags (aggressive credit estimates, no audit support, poor reviews).

When done, present the eligibility summary and comparison table to me, and then stop for human sign-off — I will make the final provider selection myself.

tax_010:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare data for our federal R&D tax credit study (Form 6765). Please pull the year's payroll data from our {{vendor}} account so we can build the engineering qualified research expense (QRE) base.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) the tax year we're claiming, (2) the list of cost centers, departments, or employee names/IDs that make up our engineering/R&D team, and (3) confirmation that you have configured credentials for {{vendor}}.

Actions to take:
1. Using your configured {{vendor}} credentials, retrieve all payroll runs for the specified tax year, either via {{vendor}}'s API or by generating and exporting payroll registers / gross-to-net reports from the dashboard.
2. Filter or tag the payroll entries down to the engineering/R&D employees I identified, capturing gross wages, employer payroll taxes, and any relevant benefits per pay period.
3. Reconcile the pulled entries against our ledger or accounting records to confirm totals match (flag any discrepancies rather than guessing).
4. Organize the output into a clean spreadsheet or CSV with columns for employee name/ID, pay period, gross wages, and total employer cost, subtotaled by employee and by pay period for the full year.

Done looks like: a single reconciled dataset covering all pay periods in the target year for the engineering/R&D population, with totals tying out to {{vendor}}'s payroll records and our ledger, ready to hand to whoever runs the QRE study.

Report back with: the file/location of the exported dataset, the total gross wages and employer payroll cost for the engineering population, any employees or pay periods you could not fully reconcile, and any assumptions you made about which employees or cost centers counted as engineering/R&D.

tax_010:n3.prompt:
You are helping me track progress on the R&D tax credit study step where our outside provider computes qualified research expenses and drafts Form 6765. The actual computation and drafting is done by the provider's own analysts on their timeline — this remains a human step that you cannot perform or accelerate.

Please do the following preparation and monitoring tasks:

1. Ask me for: the name/contact of the study provider we engaged (e.g., our accounting firm, a specialized R&D tax credit firm, or in-house tax advisor), the email thread or portal link where they're delivering the analysis, and the expected turnaround date if one was given.
2. If I have access to the provider's client portal or shared email inbox (via my configured credentials), check for status updates, requests for additional documentation (payroll records, project notes, financial statements), or a delivered draft of Form 6765.
3. If the provider has requested supporting documents from us that haven't been sent yet, help me compile a checklist of what's outstanding based on their request, and draft a reply email confirming what we're sending and asking for a revised timeline if none was given.
4. If a draft Form 6765 (and any supporting qualified research expense workpapers) has been delivered, save/organize it and summarize the key figures (total QRE, credit amount computed, any elections noted) so I can review it.
5. Set up a simple tracking note (date checked, status, next expected action) so we can monitor this until the draft arrives.

Done looks like: either (a) you've confirmed no draft has arrived yet and logged the current status and any pending action items on our side, or (b) you've retrieved and summarized a delivered draft. Report back with the current status, any outstanding items I need to send the provider, and a summary of the draft if available. Do not attempt to compute the credit yourself or fill in figures on our behalf — this is the provider's deliverable.

tax_010:n4.prompt:
You are helping me review a completed R&D tax credit study before it goes onto our federal return (Form 6765) and payroll-tax offset election (Form 8974). Ask me for: (1) the R&D study deliverable (expense schedules, qualified activity narratives, credit calculation workpapers) from whoever prepared it, (2) our payroll register or gross wages by employee for the study period, (3) our general ledger detail for contractor and supply costs claimed, and (4) the draft Form 6765 and Form 8974 if available.

Once you have these, please:
1. Cross-check every employee listed as a qualified research expense against payroll records — confirm wages match and flag any employee whose wage in the study doesn't tie to payroll data.
2. Cross-check contractor and supply expenses in the study against general ledger entries — flag any amount that doesn't reconcile.
3. Recompute the credit math (ASC or regular method, whichever was used) from the reconciled expense totals and compare it to the study's stated credit amount, flagging any variance.
4. Check that the qualified activities described are tied to specific projects/wages, not vague blanket assertions, and flag any that look unsupported.
5. Verify the payroll-tax offset amount on Form 8974 matches the credit amount claimed on Form 6765.
6. Compile a discrepancy report listing every mismatch, unsupported item, or math error found, with the underlying figures side by side.

Do not judge whether the qualified-expense classifications or credit methodology are defensible under tax law — that determination requires a tax professional's final sign-off. Prepare the reconciliation and discrepancy report, then stop for human sign-off so a qualified tax preparer or CPA can review the classifications and math before filing. Report back with the discrepancy report and a summary of what still needs professional review.

tax_010:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but not submit) IRS Form 6765 to claim the federal R&D tax credit, attached to our federal tax return, including the Form 8974 payroll-tax offset election for our pre-revenue startup.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our entity name/EIN, tax year and return type (e.g., Form 1120), our qualified research expense (QRE) documentation (wages, supplies, contract research tied to qualifying R&D activities), prior-year QRE and gross receipts data if we're using the regular credit computation, our chosen credit computation method (regular credit vs. alternative simplified credit), and confirmation of our intent to elect the payroll-tax offset under Form 8974 (including the amount we want to apply, up to the applicable annual cap).

Then: (1) Organize and summarize the qualified research expenses into the categories Form 6765 requires; (2) Fill out a draft Form 6765, using the IRS's official form at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6765.pdf as the template, computing the credit under the chosen method; (3) Fill out a draft Form 8974 reflecting the payroll-tax offset election amount; (4) Prepare a short checklist noting which supporting documentation (time tracking, expense ledgers, project descriptions) should be retained in case of audit; (5) Flag any inconsistencies or missing data you find.

Do not submit, e-file, or attach these forms to our return, and do not sign or attest to anything on my behalf — an authorized company officer must sign Form 6765 under penalties of perjury, so this remains a human step and you must stop for human sign-off once the drafts and checklist are ready.

Report back with: the completed draft forms, the QRE summary, the audit-documentation checklist, and a list of open questions or missing inputs.

tax_010:n6.prompt:
You are helping me complete the final step of claiming our federal R&D tax credit: electing the payroll-tax offset via Form 8974 and applying it inside our payroll system, {{vendor}}.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our EIN, the finalized qualified research expense (QRE) and credit amount from our completed R&D study, the Form 6765 details already attached to our filed return, our {{vendor}} login access (use my configured credentials), and the specific quarter we want the offset to begin applying against payroll taxes.

Then do the following:
1. Review the IRS Form 8974 instructions (https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8974) to confirm the reporting requirements: the credit amount, the tax period, and how it reduces the employer share of Social Security tax on Form 941.
2. Prepare a draft Form 8974 pre-filled with the QRE/credit figures I provide, showing the amount to be applied per quarter until exhausted.
3. Log into {{vendor}}'s payroll tax settings and locate the R&D payroll tax credit / offset configuration option. Enter the credit amount and effective quarter so it will automatically reduce the employer Social Security tax liability on future payroll tax filings and remittances.
4. Pull a payroll register or gross-to-net report from {{vendor}} confirming the offset is reflected correctly against upcoming payroll tax liabilities, and export it for our records.
5. Compile a checklist showing: Form 8974 draft, credit amount entered in {{vendor}}, effective quarter, and the exported report.

Done looks like: Form 8974 is drafted and ready to attach to our next Form 941, the offset is configured in {{vendor}}'s tax settings, and a report confirms the setting is active.

Since finalizing and submitting Form 8974 with the return is a filing action, stop for human sign-off before submission — report back with the completed checklist and drafted form for my review.
